clue.text: Faint suggestion that white is the winner?

definitions.meaning: to faint is to lose consciousness, to pass out

definitions.text: suggestion that white is the winner?
definitions.meaning: read as 'black (is) out', a game such as chess or draughts in which the black side has been knocked out, leaving white the victor

explanation.surface: Someone hints that the white side has won a game.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a cryptic reading of the phrase split into two words: black is out of the game.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass out is to lose consciousness, which is what fainting means.

clue.text: A fish pond could provide the fare for it

definitions.meaning: an old word for a pond where fish are kept for the table
fare means food; this is a slow-cooked dish of meat and vegetables

explanation.surface: A pond full of fish might supply the dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: The archaic sense of a fish pond is little known; the clue joins it to the everyday dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Fare is food served at a meal, and a casserole simmered in its juices is a common example; the old meaning is a fishpond.

clue.text: He works the land by a distant French sea

parts.note: distant means far away
mer is the French word for sea

explanation.surface: A man tills the soil beside a far-off French coastline.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who cultivates fields and raises crops or livestock is an agricultural worker by trade.

clue.text: It offers sole protection for the brave

definitions.text: It offers sole protection for the brave

parts.words: It offers sole protection for the brave
parts.note: brave is the old word for a Native American warrior, and the protection is for the sole of his foot: a soft leather shoe

explanation.surface: Something gives the only shield to courageous people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sole' looks like 'only' and 'brave' like 'courageous people'; really they are the underside of a foot and a warrior.
explanation.definitionFit: This soft leather slipper was worn by Native American warriors, so it protects a warrior's feet.

clue.text: Material revealing the prophet as a dupe

parts.note: a seer is a prophet who sees the future
a sucker is a dupe, someone easily fooled

explanation.surface: Some cloth exposes the soothsayer as a gullible fool.
explanation.definitionFit: This puckered striped cotton is a light fabric used for summer suits.

clue.text: Fragmented picture of Pentateuchal law

definitions.meaning: an image made of many small tiles or pieces of glass
relating to Moses, traditionally author of the first five books of the Bible, which contain the law

explanation.surface: A broken-up image of the laws of the first five books of the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture built from small fragments of stone is a tiled artwork; Mosaic law is the law given through Moses.

clue.text: No hurdles

parts.note: a horse race run with no jumps to clear, as opposed to a hurdle race or steeplechase

explanation.surface: There are no obstacles at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No hurdles' sounds like 'no difficulties', but it describes a kind of horse race.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse race on level ground with no jumps is run without obstacles.

clue.text: To practise usury is no longer wrong

parts.note: ex means former, no longer what it was
a tort is a civil wrong in law

explanation.surface: Lending at crippling interest is no longer considered sinful.
explanation.definitionFit: Charging exorbitant interest is a way of squeezing money from people, wringing it out by pressure.

clue.text: Honour Mr Todd with a Shakespearean role

parts.note: the OBE (Officer of the Order of the British Empire) is a British honour
Ron Todd was a well-known British trade union leader of the 1980s

explanation.surface: A man named Todd is decorated alongside a part in a Shakespeare play.
explanation.walkthrough: Ron Todd led the Transport and General Workers' Union; his first name is the piece wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: He is the king of the fairies in A Midsummer Night's Dream, a part in a play by the Bard.

clue.text: Small, neat lighter

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so a cow

explanation.surface: A small, tidy cigarette lighter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neat' looks like 'tidy' but is the old word for cattle; 'lighter' is not a flame but a flat-bottomed barge.
explanation.definitionFit: A lighter is a barge for unloading ships, and this flat-bottomed boat is one such vessel.

clue.text: Dated a motoring colleague in handy joint

parts.note: to date someone is to meet them romantically, so dated gives met
motoring suggests a car
a pal is a friend or colleague

explanation.surface: Someone went out with a fellow driver at a convenient pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'handy joint' sounds like a convenient place, but it means a bone of the hand.
explanation.definitionFit: These bones of the hand link wrist to fingers, so they sit at a hand joint.

clue.text: Medic imprisoned by Afrikaner terrorist, maybe

indicators.note: being imprisoned by means one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: a Boer is a South African of Dutch descent, an Afrikaner
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, stands for a doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor is held captive by a South African extremist.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who plants explosive devices is one kind of terrorist, hence the 'maybe'.

clue.text: Sue is invited to stay over

definitions.meaning: to sue is to take legal action against someone
a guest asked to stay the night packs a suitcase

explanation.surface: A woman called Sue has been asked to spend the night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sue' looks like a woman's name but is the verb to take to court.
explanation.definitionFit: To take someone to court is to launch a lawsuit; an overnight guest also arrives with luggage.

clue.text: Expedient to provide a means of support

definitions.meaning: an expedient is a device or stratagem used to deal with a difficulty
a supply of money, materials or help one can draw on

explanation.surface: Something useful to provide a way of helping.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingenious way out of trouble shows inventiveness; a supply of funds or materials is also a source of support.

clue.text: A little sweet

definitions.meaning: a small amount, as in 'a bit too much'
a British layered dessert of sponge, fruit, custard and cream

explanation.surface: A small sweet treat.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'sweet' also means a dessert course.
explanation.definitionFit: A small amount is a bit; the dessert of sponge, jelly and custard is a British pudding.

clue.text: Head leaves obsequiously, but in fine style

indicators.note: the head, or first letter, of the synonym departs from the front of that word

parts.note: slavishly means obsequiously, in a servile way

explanation.surface: A school head walks out fawningly yet elegantly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head leaves' takes S off the front of SLAVISHLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something lavishly means doing it extravagantly, sparing no expense, which is in grand style.

clue.text: Skinhead undressed and made sinuous movements

parts.note: read as the head of 'skin', its first letter
undressed means naked

explanation.surface: A shaven-headed youth stripped off and wriggled about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skinhead' is split as skin's head, giving its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To move in winding curves like a serpent is to wind sinuously.

clue.text: Problems make me dismal

indicators.note: make is read as 'are made out of' a rearrangement of the following words

explanation.surface: My troubles make me feel gloomy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make' tells you the letters of ME DISMAL are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: These are awkward choices between two bad options, which are difficulties or quandaries.

clue.text: One gripped by rage displays spirit

indicators.note: gripped by means held inside another word

parts.note: wrath means rage or great anger
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A person seized with fury shows great courage.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a ghost or apparition, a disembodied spirit.

clue.text: Display draperies the morning after

definitions.meaning: to put curtains up, letting them ... a window
the headache and nausea after a night of drinking

explanation.surface: Show off the curtains on the morning after a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Curtains hang over a rail; the after-effects of heavy drinking felt the next day are also so called.

clue.text: Begin filming when the drama's just begun!

definitions.meaning: the director's call to start a take
the point at which events start happening, when things get going

explanation.surface: Start shooting the film now the play is under way.
explanation.definitionFit: A film director's shout starts the cameras; the word also means events or activity, as in 'where the drama is'.

clue.text: Do invest sterling within limits

indicators.note: to invest is to clothe or surround, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration
L stands for the pound (libra), the unit of sterling

explanation.surface: Put some pounds into the market, but within reason.
explanation.definitionFit: Something true only to some extent is limited in degree, true in part.

clue.text: Stop the car in forward or reverse

indicators.note: the letters read the same in either direction, as a car can go forward or reverse

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Halt the vehicle whether going forwards or backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forward or reverse' looks like gears, but says the word is a palindrome.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawing a vehicle to a halt at the roadside is to bring it to a stop.

clue.text: Merchandise remains, but it's not moving

parts.note: stock is goods kept for sale
still means remains, as in 'it still exists'

explanation.surface: Unsold goods are left over, sitting idle.
explanation.definitionFit: Being motionless means completely still, without a twitch.

clue.text: Advance notice that I'm the officer in charge!

parts.note: CO stands for commanding officer
I'm gives me, the speaker

explanation.surface: Notice announcing that the speaker is the commanding officer.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a notice saying 'CO: me', the commanding officer is me.
explanation.definitionFit: To advance is to approach or move forward, to draw near.

clue.text: A lot of sailors bragged

definitions.meaning: an old past tense of crow, to boast

explanation.surface: Lots of seamen boasted.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's company is its staff of sailors; crowed, meaning boasted, has an old past tense of this form.

clue.text: Oxford detective left a little food

parts.note: Inspector Morse is the fictional detective of Colin Dexter's Oxford novels

explanation.surface: An Oxford policeman left a scrap of food on the plate.
explanation.definitionFit: A morsel is a small bite or titbit of food.

clue.text: A patient attendant so humane in disposition

indicators.note: disposition means arrangement, so the letters are set out anew

explanation.surface: A kind, patient carer, humane in temperament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'patient' looks like an adjective meaning tolerant, but it is a hospital patient; 'in disposition' rearranges SO HUMANE.
explanation.definitionFit: A junior hospital doctor in Britain is a resident who attends to people on the wards.
